title: Interactive GLSL Editor
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a split-pane layout: GLSL fragment shader code (textarea) on the left and a real-time 3D preview on the right.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Editor]
(1) Prepopulate the textarea with a simple fragment shader animation (such as a UV gradient + a time-based sine function). The vertex shader may use a default implementation or minimally pass through vUv.
(2) id="applyBtn": When clicked, compile the fragment shader code using ShaderMaterial; on success, apply it to the preview Mesh; on failure, display the compiler-returned error text in id="errorDisplay". Set hasError=false on success and hasError=true on failure.
(3) id="u_slider1", id="u_slider2", id="u_slider3": Three range sliders mapped to ShaderMaterial.uniforms (such as float values u1, u2, and u3), which may be used in the fragment shader.
(4) id="presetSelect": A <select> with at least 3 built-in shader code presets. When the selection changes, write the selected code into the textarea or apply it directly (currentPreset must be recorded in the state).
(5) id="meshSelect": A <select> with the options plane, sphere, and torus; changing the selection switches the preview geometry.

[Preview]
(6) WebGL scene on the right: Mesh + OrbitControls, updating the uTime uniform every frame.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  currentPreset: string,
  meshType: string,
  uniforms: [number, number, number],
  hasError: boolean,
  errorMessage: string,
  fps: number
}

The order of the uniforms array corresponds to the current normalized or raw values of u_slider1, u_slider2, and u_slider3 (keep this consistent with the implementation and explain it in a comment).

Output a single HTML file that can run by being opened directly in a browser.
